research.website_note: The results describe Mercury at mercury.com as a fintech company offering banking and financial software for businesses and individuals.

strategy.observation: Mercury has a very large customer base and a still-material startup base, but its growth is now coming largely from outside the AI/tech startup segment, while the product also spans multiple financial workflows like banking, cards, bill pay, invoicing, and savings.
strategy.offer_link: That mix suggests onboarding has to get new users—especially startup founders—quickly to first value across several products and use cases. A set of founder-focused onboarding email sequences could help Mercury explain the core setup path, drive early activation, and introduce the most relevant next actions by segment.
hypotheses: As Lifecycle Marketing Lead, you likely own activation, retention, and feature adoption for new customers.
Mercury may need segmented onboarding because founder startups and non-startup customers may respond to different value messages and first-use paths.
Founder users may be a strategic cohort worth nurturing into deeper adoption of Mercury’s broader product suite.
strategy.angle: Mercury is now bringing in most new customers from outside AI/tech startups, even though startups still make up a big share of your base.
strategy.fit_reason: Onboarding sequences for startup founders could be relevant because Mercury still serves a large startup audience and has multiple products to activate, but the offer is narrowly tailored to founders while Mercury’s recent growth is increasingly outside that segment, so the fit is plausible but not especially tight.

draft.subject: Founders and first value
draft.body:
Mercury is now bringing in most new customers from outside AI/tech startups, even though 1 in 3 U.S. startups still use the platform.

Given that, I wondered if the first-run experience needs to guide founder users a bit faster to their first value across banking, cards, Bill Pay, invoicing, and savings. I help teams build short onboarding email sequences that speak to startup founders, map the setup path, and set up the next best action by segment.

Would a quick look at that be useful?
